_source: Compiled 2026-11-22 for PHL model v5 from cited primary/secondary sources; 'verified' = number seen by the compiler this session at the cited URL.

premium_tertiary.definition: Log wage gap, college graduates vs high-school (secondary) graduates. 1988-95: ln(index college grad / index secondary grad), Gerochi 2002 Table 6 (earnings index, elementary grad=100; wage/salary workers 19-65, both sexes, NSO LFS Oct rounds). 2013 and 2024: composition-adjusted ratio of mean log weekly wages, college vs HS, full-time wage workers 15+ (LFS), regression on education dummies, experience, gender.
premium_tertiary.note: VERIFIED this session. Gerochi Table 6 read: sec grad 137.40/136.59/134.60, college grad 264.28/270.78/287.50 -> ln ratio 0.654/0.684/0.759 (rounded 0.65/0.68/0.76). PRWP 11163 p.8 text: 'peak of 88 percentage points in 2013', 'fell to 59 points by 2024' (80% higher wages; Fn 7). Two different methods: 1988-95 raw index (no controls, hourly/earnings unspecified) vs 2013/2024 composition-adjusted log weekly wages, so level comparability across the 1995-2013 gap is loose. Do not interpolate across the gap without a flag. Text says 2002-2007 'declined' but gives no level. Separate related estimates in premium_tertiary_alt_*.

premium_tertiary_alt_wbbrief.definition: Same WB composition-adjusted college/HS log weekly wage ratio (Fig. 5) as PRWP 11163, but values only given as rounded percent in an earlier WB policy brief; converted by me as ln(1+pct/100).
premium_tertiary_alt_wbbrief.note: Belghith, Fernandez, Jandoc, 'Structural Transformation, Job Polarization and Inequality in the Philippines' (undated policy brief, LFS 2002-21), p.5: college vs HS wage earnings 'more than 140 percent' at 2013 peak -> ln(2.40)=0.875 (lower bound; consistent with 0.88 in PRWP 11163); 'about 110 percent' in 2019 -> ln(2.10)=0.742 (rounded). Approximate; kept separate because derived from rounded percents and from a different paper.

premium_tertiary_alt_pids_full.definition: College minus secondary OLS coefficient (log hourly wage, 2018 prices; reference = no grade completed; controls sex, experience, experience^2), all salaried workers LFS. Derived by me as difference of two dummy coefficients in Albert, Punongbayan & Munoz (2024) Table 1.
premium_tertiary_alt_pids_full.note: Read Table 1 this session via fetch summariser (tables, not figure). Raw coefficients (college/secondary): 2005 1.414/0.518; 2012 1.359/0.455; 2019 1.081/0.440; 2020 0.971/0.389; 2021 0.999/0.356; 2022 0.937/0.350. Caution: the text says the 141.4% college return was in 2010 while Table 1 labels it 2005 (labelling unresolved; the summariser also flagged that text 33.7pp cumulative drop does not match Table 1). Different measure (hourly, reference no-grade, no composition adjustment beyond controls) from premium_tertiary: never splice.

premium_tertiary_alt_pids_young.note: Raw coefficients college/secondary: 2005 1.291/0.518; 2012 1.246/0.464; 2019 0.929/0.333; 2020 0.919/0.413; 2021 0.873/0.314; 2022 0.893/0.412. Reference group not stated in table (assumed no grade completed as in Table 1/Fig 1).

premium_secondary.definition: Log wage gap secondary graduate vs elementary graduate: ln(sec grad index/100), Gerochi 2002 Table 6 (wage/salary workers 19-65).

premium_secondary_alt_pids_full.definition: Secondary minus elementary OLS coefficient (reference no grade; log hourly wage), Albert et al. 2024 Table 1, all salaried workers.
premium_secondary_alt_pids_full.note: Same caveats as premium_tertiary_alt_pids_full. Note elementary here means 'some/complete elementary' dummy vs no grade, so secondary-elementary difference is not identical to Gerochi's elementary-graduate base.

formal_share.definition: Wage and salaried workers (employees) as % of total employment, WDI SL.EMP.WORK.ZS (ILO modelled estimates), 1991-2025.
formal_share.note: Values read via WebFetch of the API this session (nulls omitted; none before 1991). ILO modelled series, smooth pre-2005. Includes government employees.

urban_share.definition: Urban population share, WDI SP.URB.TOTL.IN.ZS (UN WUP-based), 1960-2025.
urban_share.note: Read via WebFetch this session. UN-based, smooth interpolation between censuses; Philippine national urban definition changes (2000s) are smoothed out.

remittances_gdp.definition: Personal remittances received, % of GDP, WDI BX.TRF.PWKR.DT.GD.ZS (BoP-based, workers' remittances and compensation of employees), 1977-2025.
remittances_gdp.note: Read via WebFetch this session. Starts 1977. Level shift 2000->2001 (8.3 -> 11.1) partly reflects a BoP methodology/coverage change (not verified).

occ_credential_share_psoc92_oct.definition: (Officials/managers/managing proprietors/supervisors + professionals + technicians & associate professionals + clerks) / total employed, October LFS rounds, PSOC-1992-style 10-group classification, PSA/NSO Table 5 'Percent distribution of employed persons by major occupation group'. Includes 'managing proprietors and supervisors' in managers, so inflated vs ISCO-08 (managers there ~ 13-16% of employment).
occ_credential_share_psoc92_oct.note: Computed by me as the sum of four published percentages per round (each rounded to 0.1, so sum error up to +/-0.2). Oct 2007 23.4; Oct 2008 24.7 (NSO, 2000-census projections); Oct 2009/2010 from the Oct 2009-10 table; Oct 2011/2012 from the Oct 2011-12 table (jump 26.6 -> 29.0 driven by managers 13.9 -> 15.9; annual 2011 managers 14.0 and annual 2012 14.9 suggest the Oct 2012 value is high relative to annual averages; reason not verified); Oct 2013/2014 exclude Leyte (13 comparable); Oct 2015 single column. Annual averages (same classification, all four rounds): 2008 24.8, 2009 26.1, 2012 28.0 (see occ_credential_share_psoc92_annual). CLASSIFICATION BREAK: before 2001 the PSA used an older 8-group scheme (see occ_credential_share_old_psoc); the 2012 PSOC (ISCO-08 aligned) series after 2015/2016 is a further break and is not spliced here.

occ_credential_share_psoc92_annual.definition: Same numerator/denominator as occ_credential_share_psoc92_oct but annual-average estimates (PSA 'Annual Estimates for Employed Persons by Industry, Occupation, Class of Worker and Hours Worked').
occ_credential_share_psoc92_annual.note: 2008: 12.7/4.5/2.6/5.0; 2009: 13.5/4.6/2.7/5.3; 2012: 14.9/4.8/2.7/5.6 (managers/professionals/technicians/clerks). 2011 annual gives only managers 14.0 in text (other groups not given). Use instead of the October series where annual averages are wanted; do not mix.
